aestheticEvaluationOrder.description: First ask whether the image has real aesthetic force: rich meaningful colour, substantial accomplished painterly execution, composed figures, believable anatomy, high religious dignity, reverent emotion. The work must be beautiful in its own right, not just illustrated subject matter.

Must invite attention, contemplation and Catholic devotion instead of looking like a generic historical engraving, institutional document, illustrative diagram, wooden mediaeval panel, flat cartoon or mundane genre scene.
Exact or honestly contextual feast, saint, mystery or Bible subevent; distinctive subject naming; no incorrect event reuse, theological distortion or misrepresenting author / medium.

Institutional original verified, photographic copy true to object, commercial-rights verified, sufficient colour/size, clean uncropped master and appropriate mobile display. These cannot rescue an aesthetically weak picture.

aestheticGradeRules.name: EXCEPTIONAL_SACRED_MASTERPIECE
aestheticGradeRules.standard: On par with user-nominated Ribalta, Rubens, Lanfranco, Navarrete and similarly rich van Dyck/Champaigne masterpieces; possible exceptional Home/Calendar anchor after approval

aestheticGradeRules.name: HIGH_QUALITY_SUPPORTING_PAINTING
aestheticGradeRules.standard: Genuinely painterly, sacred and accurate; suitable for a Bible/saint/devotion passage, but not proven exceptional enough for Home

aestheticGradeRules.name: HISTORICAL_CONTEXTUAL_ONLY
aestheticGradeRules.standard: Useful narrative or documentary material, historically relevant but less artistically compelling; never promote as an A/B sacred-art selection by filling coverage

aestheticGradeRules.name: HOLD_EXCLUDE_OR_NO_IMAGE
aestheticGradeRules.standard: Visually incompatible or already rejected, distorted subject, poor painting or image reproduction; narrative continues without image
